RR 29->30 (band=mild_tachypneic)
A 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with complaints of a sore throat and difficulty
breathing. His mother reports that the symptoms began the previous night and have worsened rapidly.
The child is normally healthy, up to date on all childhood vaccinations, and takes a daily multivitamin.
His temperature is 102.5°F (39.4°C), blood pressure is 123/71 mmHg, pulse is 137/min, respirations
are 30/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. On examination, he appears ill, is drooling, and
leans forward to breathe. He is nonverbal, visibly uncomfortable, and does not cooperate with an oral
examination. What is the most likely infectious cause of this patient’s symptoms? Answer Choices: (A)
Haemophilus influenzae (B) Streptococcus pneumoniae (C) Parainfluenza virus (D) Staphylococcus
aureus (E) Group A Streptococcus (F) Adenovirus (G) Mycoplasma pneumoniae (H) Epstein-Barr virus
(I) Corynebacterium diphtheriae (J) Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
 A. Epstein-Barr virus
B. Corynebacterium diphtheriae
C. Parainfluenza virus
D. Streptococcus pneumoniae
E. Group A Streptococcus
F. Staphylococcus aureus
G. Adenovirus
H. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
I. Haemophilus influenzae
J. Mycoplasma pneumoniae
